c.tagline: Japan's gateway to ramen and island warmth.

emergency.note: 119 covers both fire and ambulance; English-speaking operators are limited, so ask a local or hotel staff to call if possible.

hood_landmark.Hakata: Kushida Shrine, spiritual home of the Yamakasa festival
hood_landmark.Tenjin: Tenjin Chikagai, the vast underground shopping arcade
hood_landmark.Nakasu: riverside yatai food stalls lining the neon nightlife island
hood_landmark.Daimyo: boutique-lined backstreets of Fukuoka's fashion quarter
hood_landmark.Ohori: Ohori Park's lake promenade beside the Fukuoka Castle ruins

avoid.reason: Touts and inflated bar bills in the Nakasu entertainment district late at night.

hood_desc: Hakata is the transport and business hub around the main station, packed with hotels, department stores, and yatai food stalls; ideal for first-time visitors and travelers who want easy connections.
Tenjin is the buzzing downtown shopping and nightlife core with department stores, boutiques, and underground malls; suits shoppers and those wanting an energetic central base.
Nakasu is a neon-lit entertainment island famous for its riverside yatai stalls and adult nightlife; best for night owls and foodies who want atmosphere after dark.
Daimyo is a trendy, compact backstreet district full of indie boutiques, cafes, and stylish bars; appeals to younger travelers and those chasing a hip, creative vibe.
Ohori is a calm, upscale area centered on Ohori Park and its lake, near Fukuoka Castle ruins and the art museum; ideal for families and travelers seeking greenery and quiet.
lodging: The Royal Park Canvas Fukuoka Nakasu

water.note: Tap water is treated to high national standards and safe to drink straight from the tap.

transit.pay: Use a nationwide IC card such as SUGOCA, Suica or ICOCA (all interoperable) by tapping at gates and on buses; cards cost about ¥2,000 (~$13, incl. ¥500 deposit) and are sold/topped up at station machines. Base subway fares start around ¥210 (~$1.40); a 1-Day Pass (about ¥640/~$4.30) covers unlimited subway rides.
transit.hours: The subway runs daily from about 5:30am to around 12:20am.

landmarks: Fukuoka Tower
Japan's tallest seaside tower, its half-mirrored triangular glass facade glows dramatically at sunset over Momochi Beach.
Ōhori Park
A serene lake park modeled on West Lake in China, cherished for reflective water views and seasonal cherry blossoms.
Fukuoka Castle ruins
Atmospheric stone ramparts and gates within Maizuru Park, especially photogenic framed by cherry blossoms in spring.
Canal City Hakata
A vibrant shopping and entertainment complex built around a curving indoor canal, known for its bold, colorful architecture.
Dazaifu Tenmangū
A historic Shinto shrine dedicated to the god of learning, famous for its ornate shrine buildings and flowering plum trees.
Kushida Shrine
Hakata's guardian shrine, notable for its ornately decorated float displayed year-round from the Hakata Gion Yamakasa festival.
Tōchō-ji
Home to Japan's largest wooden seated Buddha statue, a striking and rarely photographed giant indoor figure.
Nokonoshima Island Park
A flower-covered island park in Hakata Bay renowned for its seasonal blooms set against sweeping sea views.
Uminonakamichi Seaside Park
A sprawling coastal national park with flower fields, a Ferris wheel, and beaches, ideal for colorful wide-angle shots.
Fukuoka PayPay Dome
A distinctive retractable-roof stadium and Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks home ground, an unmistakable landmark on the city's western skyline.

train.note: Japan is an island nation with no international trains. Hakata Station is the western terminus of the San'yo Shinkansen (to Hiroshima, Osaka and Tokyo, run by JR West) and the start of the Kyushu Shinkansen (to Kumamoto and Kagoshima, run by JR Kyushu) - book these online in English with the official SmartEX service. Conventional JR Kyushu limited expresses fan out to Nagasaki, Beppu and Miyazaki from the same station, and the Nishitetsu private line runs south from Tenjin to Dazaifu and Kurume.

bus.note: There are no international buses from Japan. Long-distance and overnight highway buses around Kyushu and to Honshu are run mainly by Nishitetsu (https://www.nishitetsu.jp/en/) and Willer Express (https://willerexpress.com/en/), leaving from the Nishitetsu Tenjin and Hakata bus terminals. Typical times are about 2 hours to Kumamoto, 2 hours 40 minutes to Beppu and 4 hours to Kagoshima, with overnight runs to Osaka and Tokyo.

intl.to: Busan (South Korea) - sails from Hakata Port International Terminal

ferry.note: The New Camellia ferry sails daily from the Hakata Port International Terminal to Busan - it departs Fukuoka during the day (about 6h) and returns overnight from Busan; bring your passport and allow time for immigration. Note that JR Kyushu's fast Queen Beetle to Busan was permanently withdrawn in December 2024, so Camellia Line is now the only direct sailing. Domestic boats from the neighbouring Bayside Place terminal serve Shikanoshima and the Genkai islands.

half.name: Itoshima

half.name: Yanagawa

full.name: Beppu

full.name: Yufuin
